lacuna.name: spec-decode-on-sm75
lacuna.repo_anchor: No plan/NNNN stage records this gap - it enters the house records only via outline.yaml item spec-decode-on-sm75 ('New from supplementation', sweep run 2026-09-07). The indirect anchors that ground it: plan/0005-format-interop/README.md line 30 records the standing rationale ('At M=1 the weight bytes match a native FP16 model's, so bandwidth-bound decode latency matches FP16 residency at half the memory') - i.e. the house already reasons about b=1 decode as a pure weight-stream, which is exactly the regime where speculative verification is near-free; plan/0007-d256-bridge/README.md carries the decode-rate rows the lever would multiply (FlashInfer d=256 baseline b=1: 16.2 tok/s at kv=1024, 11.8 at kv=4096, 5.2 at kv=16384; tp2 bridge rows swinging 12.4-16.4 tok/s across restarts) and its decode-bisect record ('the mechanism is therefore engine-level ... not the attention inner loop') - spec decode is the other engine-level decode lever, orthogonal to that campaign; and the sibling result gdn-linear-attention-sm75.json lists 'any future MTP/spec-decode work' as a consumer of the GDN microbench. MEMORY.md 2026-08-27 fixes the measurement frame: dual Quadro RTX 6000 (TU102, sm_75, 24 GB each), graphics clocks locked 1455 MHz.
lacuna.current_status: As of 2026-09-07 speculative decoding is the most active surface in LLM serving, and every method that matters is engine-level (scheduler + rejection sampler + multi-token attention plumbing), not silicon-specific. (1) EAGLE-3 (arXiv 2503.01840, 2025-03, v3 2025-04-23; SafeAI Lab - Yuhui Li, Ye Wei, Chao Zhang, Hao Zhang; NeurIPS 2025) replaced feature prediction with direct token prediction on fused multi-layer features, trained with ~8x more data under a training-time test that monitors draft/target output-distribution consistency; speedup up to 6.5x over vanilla decoding (~1.4x over EAGLE-2; ~7x in SGLang), benchmarked primarily on a single RTX 4090; draft heads train in ~24 h on one RTX 3090 for Llama3-8B/Qwen3-8B-class targets. vLLM has served it since the 0.9.x era (Red Hat write-up 2025-07-01, up to 2.5x) via method 'eagle3'. (2) P-EAGLE (vLLM blog 2026-03-13 + AWS ML blog, joint Amazon+NVIDIA team: Xin Huang, Florian Saupe, George Karypis / Benjamin Chislett, Max Xu, Omri Almog) removes EAGLE's sequential drafting bottleneck - all K draft tokens in ONE forward pass using learnable mask-token embeddings and shared hidden state - so it peaks at K=7 where vanilla EAGLE-3 peaks at K=3 (acceptance length 3.94 vs 3.03 on HumanEval at K=7); 1.05-1.69x over vanilla EAGLE-3 on GPT-OSS-20B (55-69% throughput gain at concurrency 1, 5-25% at c=64), benchmarked on a single B200; integrated from vLLM v0.16.0 (PR #32887), enabled by '"parallel_drafting": true' in the eagle3 speculative config; public parallel-trained drafter heads exist only for GPT-OSS-120B/20B and Qwen3-Coder-30B (amazon/*-p-eagle on HF). (3) MTP (DeepSeek-style, origin: DeepSeek-V3 tech report arXiv 2412.19437, 2024-12) uses the checkpoint's OWN native multi-token-prediction head as the drafter - no separate draft model to train, download, or fit in VRAM; vLLM docs gate it on 'model families that support MTP in vLLM' (latest docs name MiMo-7B and the Gemma 4 assistant checkpoints; the Qwen3-Next lineage is served via the qwen3_next/qwen3_5 family support). Qwen3-Next got native MTP serving 2025-09-11 (vLLM blog: hybrid GDN+GQA + MTP, hybrid KV-cache manager per arXiv 2503.18292, full CUDA-graph mode default for the FLA-Triton decode path). The operator's model family is fully native-MTP: Qwen3.8-27B (dense 27B, Qwen3_5ForConditionalGeneration, 48 GDN + 16 full-attention layers at interval 4, 262K native context, built-in MTP draft head) has a first-class vLLM recipe (vLLM 0.17.0+, transformers >=5.8.0): '--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' with measured acceptance 0.754-0.897 depending on quant (FP8 0.771 and NVFP4-Inferact 0.897 on 2x RTX 5090; 0.754 on 1x 5090 eager); v0.28.0 adds a DFlash parallel drafter option (incoai/Qwen3.8-27B-DFlash2, K=7). Qwen3.8-Flash-Next (a k a Qwen3.8-Next, open weights 2026-08-26, 'Qwen4 architecture preview': 125B main + 51B N-gram-embedding ultra-sparse MoE, 6B activated, 262K native context extensible to 1M via YaRN) also ships its native 1-layer MTP module with day-0 vLLM support on NVIDIA and AMD (vLLM reportedly reworked ~20,000 lines for the architecture [uncertain: figure from secondary summaries]); Unsloth reports 1.3-1.7x from MTP on it; DGX Spark ~24.1 tok/s full-model MTP3. (4) Ngram/prompt-lookup (method 'ngram', keys prompt_lookup_max/prompt_lookup_min; docs example: num_speculative_tokens 5, prompt_lookup_max 4) proposes drafts by matching n-grams in the prompt at zero model cost - the canonical lever for the operator's agent-shaped traffic; vLLM's overview additionally lists suffix decoding (dynamic depth, no extra model), PARD parallel drafts, MLP speculators, dynamic speculative decoding and adaptive verification. (5) The failure-mode literature is equally mature: vLLM #21278 (2025-07-21, closed not-planned/stale with zero maintainer response) shows a Qwen3-4B-FP8 draft DEGRADING a Qwen3-32B-FP8 target from 20-21 to 10-11 tok/s on 2x L20 (v0.9.2, num_spec=3) - separate-draft-model TP overhead plus weak acceptance eats the gain; the docs position all of it as 'reduce inter-token latency under medium-to-low QPS, memory-bound workloads'. (6) What does NOT exist anywhere: a Turing-class (T4/2080Ti/RTX 6000) spec-decode benchmark from any upstream project - the only public sm_75 spec-decode numbers are the weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive fork's own docs (below), which is the gap this item names.
lacuna.sm75_viability: ENGINE-LEVEL METHODS RUN ON TURING UNMODIFIED - nothing in EAGLE-3/P-EAGLE/MTP/ngram checks compute capability; the plumbing is scheduler + rejection sampler + multi-token attention, all torch/CUDA-graph level. The one proven sm_75 deployment is weicj/vLLM-2080Ti-Definitive (base vLLM 0.21.0, fork v0.1.17, runtime vllm-sm75-tp2-cu128, CUDA 12.8/torch 2.11.0): MTP3 is a first-class green route on Qwen3.6/3.8-27B across KV dtypes, shipped as launcher profiles (e.g. qwen27b/normal/int4/fp16kv-256K-mtp3-text-only.env), with CUDAGraph green for FP16-KV and TurboQuant-KV routes and partial for INT8-KV. Its docs/mtp-task-sensitivity.md is THE Turing spec-decode dataset: Qwen3.6-27B-GPTQ-INT4 on dual 2080 Ti aggregate 43.59 -> 60.62 tok/s (1.39x; science 1.45x, code 1.39x, prose 1.34x) at MTP3; Qwen acceptance decays 87.0% (K=1) -> 67.9% (K=3) -> 51.3% (K=5) - the reason MTP3 is its recommended mixed-workload default; Gemma4-31B gets only 1.07x aggregate with prose REGRESSING to 0.89x (acceptance 63.5% at K=3, 29.9% at K=10) - task sensitivity is real and quantified. Community corroboration: ~40 tok/s Q4/100K-ctx/MTP on a single 22GB 2080 Ti (NxCode write-up), 60.8 -> ~74 tok/s on a Qwen3.8-27B MTP setup (Reddit), DGX-Spark MTP3 4.5 -> 9.9 TPS (2.2x) as the low-bandwidth extreme. THE ACCEPTANCE x DRAFT-COST MATH ON FMA/CUDA KERNELS, which no upstream benchmark supplies for Turing: at b=1 the decode step is a pure weight stream (plan/0005's own M=1 argument), so verifying gamma+1 tokens instead of 1 costs almost nothing extra - a GEMV with M=4 vs M=1 adds FLOPs that are free under the bandwidth roof whether the kernel is FMA or mma-based, and Turing's tensor cores idle at M=1 anyway; speedup therefore reduces to tau/(1 + c*gamma) with tau = (1-alpha^(gamma+1))/(1-alpha) (Leviathan et al., arXiv 2211.17192) and c = per-draft-step cost in target-forward units. Back-computing from weicj's own numbers - alpha = 0.679 at K=3 gives tau = 2.45 tokens/step, measured 1.39x implies c ~ 0.25 target-forwards per MTP draft step on sibling silicon [uncertain: derived, conflates the shared-lm_head stream, the draft layer's own KV/GDN ops, scheduler and host overhead] - i.e. the draft step costs ~25% of a target step, NOT the naive 1/64-layer estimate, because the MTP head re-streams the big vocab projection per drafted token; this is also why P-EAGLE's one-pass drafting (K drafts in 1 forward) and ngram (zero drafting cost) are the structurally right answers for memory-bound parts. #21278 is the cautionary tale for the separate-draft-model route: a 4B draft under TP2 paid three sequential draft streams plus per-step all-reduces and halved throughput - avoid separate drafts on this host, or pin draft_tensor_parallel_size=1. METHOD MATRIX FOR THIS HOST: (a) MTP on Qwen3.8-27B - the family-native path; needs the qwen3_next/qwen3_5 MTP model code (vLLM 2025-09+ / 0.17.0+ for Qwen3.8), draft weights load from the same checkpoint (no extra VRAM beyond ~1 layer + shared head), expected 1.3-1.45x per weicj's sibling-silicon measurements; (b) ngram - zero-cost drafts, ideal for agent/code/repetitive traffic, method-level only, helps exactly where MTP acceptance is weakest; (c) EAGLE-3 - NO official Qwen3-family draft exists (yuhuili ships LLaMA-family only; XLOverflow community drafts for Qwen3-8B; TW-EAGLE3 for Qwen3-Coder 1.37x; SpecForge arXiv 2603.18567 exists because 'many mainstream models, including Qwen3, lack publicly available matching draft models'), so it means training a Qwen3.8-27B head (~24 h on one 3090 for 8B-class [uncertain: 27B-class on the fork's 2x24 GB host]) for strictly less convenience than native MTP; (d) P-EAGLE - best structural fit for deep K (draft cost independent of K) but needs a v0.16.0-class engine base AND a parallel-trained drafter that exists publicly only for GPT-OSS and Qwen3-Coder-30B. VERIFICATION-KERNEL INTERACTION ON THE FORK (the one real kernel-side gate): the verify pass issues q_len = K+1 query tokens through decode attention - the plan/0006/0007 d128/d256 decode-shaped kernels are q_len=1 instantiations, so verification either routes through FlashInfer/TRITON_ATTN decode (both handle q>1; the fork's FlashInfer sm75 line does BatchDecode with multi-token queries) or the fork kernels need a q_len>1 variant [uncertain: current kernels' q>1 support not verified in repo records]. HYBRID KV-LAYOUT INTERACTION (48-GDN/16-full-attention): full-attention layers' KV grows K+1 tokens per step under the hybrid KV-cache manager (arXiv 2503.18292 - logical block sizing equalizes GDN state and full-attn KV physical pages), while the GDN recurrent state is fixed-size per sequence and MUST be checkpointed at the draft boundary and rolled back on partial rejection - vLLM implements this for the qwen3_next family, and it is the fragile edge: #40756 (open, 2026-04-24, v0.19.1, Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 tp4, num_spec=5) crashes with illegal memory access past ~26K total tokens, preceded by acceptance spiking to 100% and scheduled draft tokens going -1 at gpu_model_runner _prepare_input_ids; #40831 (2026-04-24) shows TurboQuant-KV x MTP emitting degenerate loops ('<tool_call>' repeats, NIA 'amber amber amber') on a Qwen3.6-27B hybrid at 2x3090 because draft and verify read the SAME dequantized cache, so the corrupted distribution matches across both and looping drafts get silently accepted (workaround: fp8_e5m2 KV or drop spec, 85 -> 40 tok/s). CUDA-GRAPH COMPATIBILITY: upstream runs the FLA decode path under full CUDA-graph mode by default for qwen3_next and extends the capture range by K x max_num_seqs for spec decode; capture memory is budgeted OUTSIDE gpu-memory-utilization (recipe case: 784 MiB capture OOM on a 32GB 5090 forcing --enforce-eager) - tight but workable on 24 GB Turing cards since the MTP head is one layer; the weicj fork runs CUDAGraph green on its MTP3 profiles and warns that thermal throttling masquerades as software regression during repeated graph/AOT capture - the locked-1455 MHz discipline already neutralizes that on this host. Attention-backend candidate matrix where it gates this item: verification decode q>1 works on FlashInfer (fork's pre-v0.24 line) and TRITON_ATTN (FMA-bound but correctness-fine at q=4); FA2 is disqualified on this host already (plan/0007 gate-0); the GDN side rides FLA fused_recurrent (graph-friendly) regardless of method.

effort_value.effort_estimate: NOT a kernel campaign - this is an engine-configuration-plus-validation item with one bounded kernel-side contingency. Sizing: (1) MTP3 enablement on the Qwen 27B route: wire the speculative config through the fork's engine (the qwen3_next/qwen3_5 MTP model code exists upstream from 2025-09+; if the fork's base predates it, this rides the drift row's planned v0.23.0-class rebase rather than being new work), verify draft-head loading from the checkpoint, extend CUDA-graph capture sets to the K+1 decode shapes - 1-2 sessions; (2) correctness/gate suite (the real work, gate-0 style): greedy no-MTP vs MTP output-equality oracle, GDN state rollback stress (forced rejections), long-context >26K sweep (#40756 tripwire), tool-call/NIA real-prompt traces (#40831 tripwire), KV-dtype x MTP interaction matrix - 1-2 sessions; (3) timing ladder: K sweep (MTP1/3/5) reproducing the acceptance-decay curve, task-sensitivity rows (science/code/prose) against the weicj table, ngram A/B on agent traces - 1 session under exclusive lease + median-of-N across restarts; (4) contingency kernel row ONLY IF verification cannot route through FlashInfer/TRITON decode: a q_len>1 variant of the d128 decode-shaped kernel - bounded, plan/0006-pattern work, +2-3 sessions. EAGLE-3-on-Qwen3.8 (train a draft head) and P-EAGLE (train a parallel drafter + v0.16.0 base) are separate campaigns the probe should explicitly NOT open unless MTP+ngram underdeliver.
effort_value.unlocks: The single largest remaining engine-level multiplier on the operator's serving target: single-stream decode on the 27B hybrid at 1.3-1.45x (weicj's sibling-silicon measurements; the plan/0007 rows 16.2/11.8/5.2 tok/s by context would become ~22/16/7 class, and the kv=16384 long-context row - exactly where #47549-style capacity pain lives - benefits most since verification is free under the bandwidth roof while accepted tokens amortize the weight stream). MTP costs no extra VRAM-resident model (head ships in the checkpoint) and no KV growth per accepted token - unlike batching, it multiplies tok/s without touching the KV-capacity envelope that the engine-kv-capacity item treats as first-class. Ngram adds a zero-cost second lever aimed at the operator's agent traffic (tool-call echoes, code re-edits, few-shot repetition) precisely where MTP acceptance decays. Method-gate unlocks: settles whether the fork's decode kernels need q_len>1 (a requirement spec for the paged-varlen-decode item too), hardens the GDN rollback semantics the GDN microbench item flagged, and gives the fork the only public Turing spec-decode reference numbers in existence - the gap the outline itself names.
effort_value.dependency_order: External prerequisites: the fork's engine base must carry qwen3_next-family MTP code (vLLM 2025-09+ line; v0.17.0+ for Qwen3.8-27B architecture support, v0.16.0+ if P-EAGLE is ever wanted) - this is the drift row's rebase decision, already teed up; draft weights come free with the Qwen3.8 checkpoint; ngram needs nothing. Repo-internal: nothing must land first - the oracle harness (plan/0003/0007), the locked-clock lease discipline, and the acceptance-rate telemetry pattern (spec_decode_num_accepted/draft_tokens_total metrics) all exist; the 27B engine itself is plan/0007-delivered. Ordering interaction that matters: the tp2 decode-variance bisect is RED and open, and spec decode changes the decode step shape (K+1 tokens, extra draft kernels, larger capture sets) - land or explicitly fence that bisect FIRST, or the first MTP timing rows will be confounded by the same 12.4-16.4 restart swing; conversely MTP-off rows are unaffected, so the campaigns can proceed in parallel if all spec rows are judged on cross-restart medians from day one. The KV-quant items (fp8-kv, TurboQuant integration) are consumers of this item's interaction matrix, not blockers. The optional q_len>1 kernel contingency depends on the attention-routing decision inside the probe itself.
effort_value.risk_notes: Correctness risk is the headline, and it is proven-in-the-wild, not hypothetical: (1) #40831 - KV quantization x MTP on the 27B hybrid produced SILENT degenerate loops because draft and verify read the same dequantized cache, so the corrupted distribution matched across both and looping drafts were accepted; short narrative/code outputs looked normal while tool-calls and needle-in-haystack broke - repeated-token synthetic tests PASS under this bug class (weicj's own doc says validate with real prompts, not repeated-token synthetics), so the gate suite must include real-prompt NIA/tool-call traces with acceptance-rate anomaly asserts. (2) #40756 - MTP at num_spec=5 crashes with illegal memory access past ~26K tokens on Qwen3.6-27B-FP8 (open, v0.19.1) - long-context sweeps are mandatory before any 256K-context MTP route is trusted on this host. (3) Acceptance-rate telemetry can lie (the 100%-acceptance spike before the crash) - treat monotone-sane acceptance decay (the 87/68/51% K-curve) as a health invariant, not just a perf number. Numerics: the MTP head rides the same fp16-recast contract as the target on Turing (no bf16); rejection sampling preserves the target distribution ONLY if the sampler is exactly right - greedy output-equality against no-MTP is the cheap losslessness oracle. Performance/footguns: prose-heavy or non-Qwen targets can REGRESS (Gemma4-31B 0.89x on prose) - task-sensitivity must be measured, not assumed; separate draft models under TP halved throughput (#21278) - do not take that route; CUDA-graph capture allocates outside the memory budget (784 MiB OOM case on a 32GB card) and thermal throttling masquerades as regression during repeated capture (weicj warning; locked 1455 MHz neutralizes); host CPU can bound the route (weicj saw 91 vs 56 tok/s MTP3 across hosts). Upstream-drift exposure: the machinery is fast-moving (P-EAGLE 2026-03, DFlash 2026-08, suffix decoding new) and the bug window (#40756 open) means the fork pins a specific base and carries its patches forward - fork-maintained forever once deviating from upstream spec-decode internals.
effort_value.determinism_class: Two-layer classification. (1) Algorithmic: speculative decoding is lossless BY CONSTRUCTION under correct rejection sampling - greedy (temperature=0) spec-decode output must be BITWISE-IDENTICAL to greedy no-spec output given pinned kernels; that equality is the oracle (the float64-reference discipline maps to output-equality plus the existing PPL gates, since the target model's kernels are unchanged). Temperature>0 runs are stochastic BY DESIGN (sampling RNG plus rejection resampling) - gate those on distributional agreement across many samples, never bitwise. (2) Mechanical: the MTP path adds no atomics and no split-K - fixed-order FMA/CUDA kernels, deterministic CUDA-graph replays - so run-to-run variance sources are the ones the house already polices: engine-restart scheduling state (the plan/0007 tp2 lesson - judge on medians across >=3 restarts), Triton autotune cache selection on any Triton-touched leg (pin/log configs per transcript), and graph-capture set membership. Restart-to-restart acceptance-rate variance is a SAMPLING statistic, not nondeterminism - median-of-N with the acceptance-decay curve as sanity band; the float64-oracle + median-of-N discipline holds unchanged, with one addition: acceptance-rate anomalies (spikes to 100%, scheduled-draft -1s) are recorded as correctness tripwires per #40756, and replay-affecting state (GDN recurrent snapshots) is assert-checked against recompute-from-scratch on forced-rejection traces.

decision.priority_signal: FOR doing this next: it is the highest-ratio lever left on the operator's target - engine-level (no kernel campaign), family-native (Qwen3.8-27B ships the MTP head; no draft to train, download, or fit), proven on sibling Turing silicon (weicj: 1.39x aggregate, 1.45x science, acceptance 67.9% at K=3), and structurally ideal for memory-bound b=1 decode where verification rides the same weight stream for free while Turing's idle-at-M=1 tensor cores make the FMA-vs-mma question irrelevant to the marginal verify cost; ngram is a free second lever for the agent traffic; nothing upstream will ever supply Turing spec-decode numbers, so the fork owns the reference row. AGAINST / ordering: the tp2 decode-variance bisect is RED and open, and MTP changes the decode step shape that campaign is instrumenting - sequencing matters or both campaigns blur; #40756 is an OPEN upstream crash on exactly the target model family at long context, so the correctness suite is load-bearing before any timing claim; the KV-quant interaction (#40831) means the fp8-kv/TurboQuant ambitions must be co-designed with MTP or explicitly fenced; P-EAGLE/EAGLE-3 routes lack Qwen3.8-matched draft weights and add training campaigns the probe should not open. Window: the ecosystem is converging on spec decode as the default serving posture (P-EAGLE mainline 2026-03, DFlash 2026-08, Qwen shipping MTP heads natively) - a fork without it drifts from 'serving' to 'limping' on 24 GB cards. Net: do it right after (or fenced-parallel with) the tp2 bisect, MTP3-first, ngram alongside, EAGLE-3/P-EAGLE explicitly out of scope.
decision.recommended_probe: Gate-0 style, oracle-first, no timing until numerics are green - roughly 2-3 sessions on the existing dual-RTX-6000 host. (1) ENABLE: run the Qwen 27B route with '--speculative-config '{"method":"mtp","num_speculative_tokens":3}' through the fork's engine (post-rebase if the base lacks qwen3_next MTP code), CUDAGraph on, acceptance telemetry (spec_decode_num_{accepted,draft}_tokens_total) logged per step. (2) ORACLE SUITE before any timing: (a) greedy equality - temperature-0 MTP output must match temperature-0 no-MTP output byte-for-byte across 50+ real prompts (science/code/prose per the weicj task split); (b) forced-rejection GDN rollback - high-temperature and deliberately-corrupted draft seeds, asserting the recurrent state after partial rejection equals recompute-from-scratch; (c) long-context sweep to >32K total tokens (the #40756 tripwire: assert no illegal access, acceptance stays in the sane decay band, no scheduled-draft -1s); (d) real-prompt NIA and tool-call traces (the #40831 tripwire: no loops) across KV dtypes in the fork's matrix (fp16, int8, any quantized-KV candidate) - any loop or distributional anomaly disqualifies that KV x MTP combination outright. (3) ONLY THEN TIME, exclusive lease, locked 1455 MHz, medians across >=3 engine restarts, warmup/graph-capture excluded per the weicj methodology note: K sweep at 1/3/5 to reproduce the acceptance-decay curve (expect ~0.87/0.68/0.51 Qwen-class), tok/s vs the plan/0007 baseline rows at kv=1024/4096/16384, and the back-computed draft-cost c (tau/(1+c*gamma)) to characterize the fork's own MTP-head cost; ngram A/B on 10 agent traces (prompt_lookup_max 3-6) at zero model cost. (4) ROUTING CHECK: confirm which decode attention serves the q=K+1 verification pass (FlashInfer vs TRITON vs fork kernel) via a one-step profile; only if it falls off the fast path does the q_len>1 kernel contingency open. Deliverable: a dated ledger row (acceptance, tok/s by task and K, draft-cost c, KV-interaction verdicts, verification-routing verdict) that either closes the item ('MTP3+ngram green, 1.3-1.4x banked, kernel contingency not needed') or scopes the one bounded follow-up with a number.
